title: MapQuest MCP for Claude — location-aware agents that route your day
summary: Plugging the MapQuest MCP server into Claude gives the model real place search, distances, travel times and traffic, so it can order a day's stops into a sensible route instead of listing random recommendations. Same server works for any agent that needs geography; MapQuest offers 50,000 free transactions to start.
takeaways: Add a geo MCP server and the agent can optimize multi-stop itineraries by real travel time, not vibes.
The pattern generalizes: delivery planning, field-sales routes, local-search agents.
MapQuest's free tier (50k transactions) is enough to prototype.

title: PostHog interest-segmented landing pages — personalize by visitor behavior
summary: Sponsored PostHog post: install PostHog, let two weeks of visitor sessions accumulate, then prompt an AI to cluster visitors into interest groups (e.g. sales vs. support features) and generate a landing-page variant per group that returning visitors see. Also argues flashy animated landing templates convert poorly.
takeaways: Segment returning visitors by first-click behavior and serve a tailored page.
Animated templates can hurt conversion; measure before shipping looks.
This is a paid ad (#teamposthog); prompts gated behind a comment.

title: GPT-6 Astra + Codex one-person company — context files and daily checkpoints
summary: Set up a workspace with three markdown context files (aboutme.md built from a 20-question interview, an anti-AI writing-style ban list, and mycompany.md with model, revenue and quarterly goals), then run Codex on GPT-6 Astra at three daily checkpoints: 8am inbox triage and call prep, noon delegation to sub-agents, 5pm audit whose summary seeds tomorrow's context.
takeaways: Give the model persistent identity/style/business context files instead of long prompts.
A banned-phrases style file is the cheapest fix for AI-sounding output.
End-of-day audit summaries become next-day context: a continuous memory loop.

title: Katana crawler — JavaScript endpoint discovery and deep-crawl flags
summary: Part two of a Katana walkthrough: use the JavaScript-crawl flag to pull endpoints out of JS files that a basic crawl misses, set crawl depth with -d, and write results to a file. Demoed against a local CTF VM; only for systems you own or are authorized to test.
takeaways: Enable JS crawling to surface hidden API routes during recon.
Increase -d depth for thorough crawls and save output for later fuzzing.
Practice on CTF boxes, not third-party sites.

title: NFC stickers + vibe-coded web app — physical taps that log real-life habits
summary: Programmable NFC stickers on a water bottle trigger an Apple Shortcut that logs each finished bottle to a tiny Next.js/TypeScript web app, surfaced as a home-screen widget. Part two of an IRL vibe-coding series; next step is a Raspberry Pi force sensor to log automatically.
takeaways: NFC sticker + Shortcuts + a simple web endpoint = one-tap physical logging.
Physical triggers make boring tracking effortless.
Upgrade path: sensors (force/weight) on a Raspberry Pi for passive capture.

title: Overnight return anomaly — most stock gains accrue close-to-open
summary: Cites research showing that across global markets most equity returns come overnight (close to next open) while intraday holding loses; the Micron example claims +138M% overnight vs −99% intraday on paper. Proposed mechanism: retail trades the open, institutions trade into the close. Paper not named; frictions and costs ignored.
takeaways: Decompose any strategy's returns into overnight and intraday legs.
Close-to-open holding is a testable edge; costs and gap risk decide if it survives.
Look up the 'tug of war' overnight-returns literature before trusting the headline numbers.

title: x402 protocol — pay-per-crawl tolls for AI agents scraping your site
summary: Frames the AI scraping lawsuits (Anthropic's ~$1.5B author settlement, NYT v. OpenAI) as a payment problem and points to x402, a 2025 protocol that revives the long-dormant HTTP 402 Payment Required status so agents pay a crypto micropayment to access content. Explanation is hype-heavy and ends in a paid Skool pitch.
takeaways: x402 lets a site charge AI agents per request using stablecoin payments.
Watch it as a monetization layer for content and APIs consumed by agents.
The '1991 slot' is HTTP status 402, reserved but unused until protocols like x402.

title: AI Overview SEO — seeding social posts that Google and ChatGPT cite
summary: A LinkedIn post declaring someone 'the world's most renowned AI visibility expert' was cited by Google's AI Overview the same day. Lesson: user-generated platforms (YouTube, Reddit, LinkedIn, X) dominate citations, so lead posts with your keyword and backlink them to keep them cited. Ends in a promo for compactkeywords.com.
takeaways: AI answer engines lean heavily on UGC platforms for citations.
Put the target keyword at the start of the post.
Shows how easily AI Overviews can be gamed with self-assertion.

title: Microduck robot — reinforcement learning with PPO and reward shaping
summary: Training Pollen Robotics' open-source Microduck to stand: define a reward function (e.g. points for target body height), simulate 4,096 parallel robots, and let PPO update the policy toward higher-reward actions. The result 'stands' in an unintended way, a clean demo of reward hacking and why reward design is iterative.
takeaways: RL = reward function + many parallel simulated attempts + policy updates.
Agents exploit loose rewards; expect to iterate on reward terms.
Microduck is an approachable open-source RL playground.

title: GPT-6 Astra prompt pack — comment-bait with no content
summary: Caption teases GPT-6 Astra prompts for Codex/ChatGPT behind a comment keyword; the audio is just music, so the post carries no actual prompts or technique.
takeaways: Nothing to extract; content gated behind DM.
Dropped as pure promo.
drop_reason: pure self-promo, zero content (audio is music, prompts gated)

title: GPT-6 Astra stock-trading challenge — scheduled Codex tasks in one thread
summary: Creator gives GPT-6 Astra $10k to trade, rerunning an earlier Claude experiment that reportedly beat the S&P by 8% in a month. Six scheduled Codex tasks per day read news, open, review and manage positions, all posting into one shared thread for visibility. No results yet; setup doc gated behind a comment.
takeaways: Single shared thread for all scheduled agent runs makes reasoning auditable.
One-month S&P outperformance is noise, not evidence.
Structure: news read, entry, review, management as separate scheduled checks.

title: Herk Brain AI OS — local knowledge graph wired into a personal dashboard
summary: A local folder-based 'AI operating system' links business wiki, meetings, video knowledge, Claude/Codex memory, projects, skills and agents into one graph, then exposes it through a personal OS dashboard (calendar, Slack/ClickUp/email replies, meeting action items, YouTube comment trends). A free GitHub repo interviews you and scaffolds the same setup, 3D brain view included.
takeaways: Keep all context as local files so any model can be pointed at it.
An interview-driven setup repo is a good onboarding pattern for personal agents.
Unify comms, meetings and audience signals in one agent-readable dashboard.

title: Stay-secure privacy checklist — de-dox yourself from AI and data brokers
summary: After Meta AI pieced together a creator's home location from old posts, this free browser-only checklist walks you through mapping your accounts, auditing what's public, opting out of data brokers and ad trackers, credit freezes, recovery codes, tracking who holds your ID, and identity-theft recovery.
takeaways: AI assistants can now correlate old posts into a home address; audit your footprint.
Opt out of data brokers and freeze credit; both are free.
The checklist runs entirely in your browser with no account.

title: GPT-6 Astra web design skill — layered parallax hero sections in one shot
summary: Showcase of one-shot landing pages from GPT-6 Astra using the creator's design skill: multi-layer parallax scroll scenes, 3D product elements that morph on scroll, minimal premium sections below. Visual reference only; the skill is gated behind a comment.
takeaways: Separate subject, ground, map and text into layers for depth on scroll.
Dynamic hero, calm minimal sections below is a strong default.
Skill itself isn't shared publicly.

title: Three cybersecurity portfolio projects — fuzzing, agent sandboxing, YARA scanning
summary: Portfolio ideas that signal real skill: a fuzzer that hammers C libraries with malformed files to find memory-corruption crashes; an AI agent guard that assumes prompt injection will succeed and limits what the agent may do; and a static binary scanner that matches detection rules and explains each hit. Source links gated behind a comment.
takeaways: Prompt injection can't be filtered reliably; contain what the agent can do.
Fuzzing C libraries is how memory-corruption bugs get found.
Build projects that show exploitation-relevant skills, not tutorials.

title: ChatGPT warm-referral job hunt — mutual connections to bypass ATS filters
summary: Sponsored ChatGPT post: have ChatGPT find the recruiter and hiring manager for a role, list your mutual connections in a spreadsheet, message those contacts asking to use their name, then run a scheduled task that drafts a name-drop email to the hiring manager when they say yes.
takeaways: Referrals beat resume filters; automate finding mutual connections.
Use a scheduled check for replies before sending the hiring-manager email.
Paid partnership with ChatGPT (#ad).

title: UX laws cheat sheet — 20 rules to feed Claude as design instructions
summary: Rapid list of UX principles meant to be dropped into a markdown instruction file for Claude: fewer choices per screen, large targets, familiar patterns, chunking, sub-400ms response, clear primary action, visible progress, sensible defaults, error prevention and recovery, progressive disclosure, and goal-gradient framing.
takeaways: Encode UX laws in a CLAUDE.md-style file so generated UIs follow them.
Respond within 400ms; show progress; make errors recoverable.
Reveal complexity gradually and make completion feel close.

title: Four GitHub design repos — R3F, liquid glass, shader gradients, liquid chrome
summary: Treat GitHub as a designer's asset library: React Three Fiber for Three.js 3D, liquid-glass-js for Apple-style liquid glass, ShaderGradient for animated customizable gradients in React, and Liquid Logo for a chrome liquid-metal effect. Point Claude Code or Codex at a repo, check licence and maintenance, and adapt the smallest effect in a throwaway branch.
takeaways: Point a coding agent at a repo and describe the effect you want.
Check licence, maintenance and framework before adopting.
Isolate one effect in a disposable branch before merging.

title: MLS API rental finder — bypass Zillow with your own listings pipeline
summary: Get MLS data via API by registering as a vendor sponsored by a realtor friend, then prompt an AI to build a workflow that pulls listings matching your filters into your own database and emails each listing agent to express interest. Idea credited to another builder.
takeaways: Direct MLS access shows listings aggregators bury.
Pipe filtered listings into your own DB, then automate agent outreach.
Needs a sponsoring licensed realtor for access.

title: Soup — fine-tune LLMs on a 4GB laptop GPU with one command
summary: Soup, built by a 17-year-old solo founder from Kazakhstan, wraps LLM fine-tuning into a simple flow: describe the goal, point at your data, run `soup train`, and it auto-picks batch size and memory settings. Claimed 85k users training medical assistants and reasoning models on consumer GPUs. Link gated; verify the claims.
takeaways: Small-model fine-tuning is feasible on 4GB VRAM with auto-configured settings.
Good fit for domain assistants trained on your own data.
Viral-claim post; check the actual repo and benchmarks first.

title: Gestural agent interface — TouchDesigner concept for hand-commanded AI
summary: Non-functional TouchDesigner prototype imagining agentic UI driven by gestures: two running fingers run the program, spinning fingers spin up a new idea, a pinch delegates heavy lifting.
takeaways: Map metaphorical gestures to agent verbs (run, ideate, delegate).
Useful speculative reference for non-chat agent UIs.

title: ARRAY circular edition — TouchDesigner light-art process
summary: Process glimpse from perspek.steven's ARRAY series: a circular light-art piece built and sequenced in TouchDesigner. Silent visual reference for generative lighting and new-media installation work.
takeaways: Reference for circular LED/light array compositions driven by TouchDesigner.
Study the build process to see how sequenced light patterns are composed.

title: Bending Spoons playbook — AI-native acquisitions of stagnant SaaS
summary: Bending Spoons grew from $40k to an $18B IPO by buying stagnating platforms (Evernote, Vimeo, Meetup, WeTransfer) cheaply, rebuilding only the core features customers use with a lean elite engineering team, cutting cost base and compounding margin into the next deal. Argues AI-native acquirers, not vendors, are the new playbook PE/VC is funding.
takeaways: Buying a cash-flowing product and rebuilding the core leanly can beat building new.
Margin expansion is the strategy, not the side effect.
AI lowers the cost of rebuilding legacy software.
